rounds.text: Sattva Sukun Lifecare Ltd is profoundly under-appreciated because its top-line expansion is operating at an extraordinary velocity that the market price fails to reflect. Compounded sales growth has surged to 90% over 5 years [E13], accelerated further to 144% over 3 years [E14], and reached a staggering 447% over the trailing twelve months [E15], supported by screening signals confirming accelerating earnings growth [E59]. This immense commercial momentum is available at a deep discount, with the stock trading at a price-to-book ratio of just 0.65x against a book value of ₹ 1.13 [E1], which is radically lower than the sector benchmark P/B of 3.77x [E6]. Furthermore, the company maintains a positive return on assets of 0.03%, vastly outperforming the sector benchmark of -171.35% [E7]. Conceded: compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months has dropped by -103% [E18], and the P/E ratio sits at an elevated 77x compared to the sector benchmark of 35.78x [E5].

Sattva Sukun Lifecare Ltd presents a severe disconnect between its lofty earnings multiple and its actual profitability, trading at a P/E of 77x against a sector benchmark of 35.78x [E5]. This excessive valuation is entirely unsupported by the company's returns on equity, delivering a meager ROE of 0.25% compared to the sector benchmark of 30.31% [E8]. Compounded profit growth has deteriorated significantly, contracting by 24% over 5 years, 43% over 3 years, and plunging by 103% over the trailing twelve months [E16, E17, E18]. Furthermore, the company offers a dividend yield of 0.00%, returning nothing to shareholders while they shoulder these operational declines [E3]. Conceded: price-to-book is 0.65x on a book value of ₹ 1.13 [E1].
